channel.title: VISIONE Wire
channel.description: High-signal reporting and original analysis on AI, software, computing infrastructure, cybersecurity, digital business and technology policy.

item.title: Amazon ties up to $60 billion of AI-chip spending to Qualcomm
item.description: Amazon's Qualcomm agreement links up to $60 billion of purchases to custom AI server silicon, giving AWS another path to diversify inference infrastructure.

item.title: Mistral raises €3 billion as Europe turns AI sovereignty into a capital race
item.description: Mistral's Series D nearly doubles its post-money valuation in a year and gives Europe's flagship frontier-AI company fresh capital for research, compute and infrastructure.

item.title: Liquid Network pauses after roughly $320 million in bitcoin is withdrawn
item.description: Liquid Network paused after roughly 4,000 BTC, worth about $320 million, was withdrawn from its federation wallet while the root cause remains unresolved.

item.title: OpenAI says it has reached its automated research-intern milestone
item.description: OpenAI says its coding agents can now handle well-defined research tasks that would take a skilled researcher days, while aggregate agent runtime has overtaken human labor in its research organization.

item.title: U.S. government backs OpenAI in New York Times copyright case
item.description: A federal filing argues that courts should not treat training large language models on copyrighted text as automatically unlawful.

item.title: Dell raises FY2027 outlook as AI server backlog reaches $95 billion
item.description: Dell booked $60.9 billion in AI server orders in one quarter, ended with a $95 billion AI backlog and raised its full-year revenue forecast to $192 billion.

item.title: Anthropic details security overhaul after Claude agents accessed real systems
item.description: Anthropic says it paused high-risk AI training and cyber evaluations after unauthorized agent actions, then added real-time blockers, stronger sandboxes and tighter monitoring.

item.title: Europe orders €387.8 million LUMI-AI supercomputer with AMD MI430X GPUs
item.description: EuroHPC has signed a €387.8 million contract for a Finland-based AI supercomputer expected to deliver a major increase in European public compute capacity.

item.title: Opera loses EU court challenge over Microsoft Edge DMA exemption
item.description: The EU General Court upheld the Commission's decision that Microsoft Edge is not an important gateway under the Digital Markets Act.

item.title: U.S. pushes G20 toward lighter AI regulation with Carolina Principles
item.description: Washington is urging G20 governments to avoid broad new AI-specific rules and regulators unless genuinely new risks demand them.
